Bluff ShowProject record · built 2026-09-17 from feat/bluff-show-v1

Bluff Show

A Fibbage-style bluffing trivia party game in the browser for 3–10 players, styled as a 70s TV quiz show. Each round shows a strange-but-true fact with a blank; everyone writes a fake answer, the fakes are mixed with the truth, and players score for finding the truth (+1000) and for fooling others (+500 per player fooled, double in the last round). Two modes: pass one device around, or host a room on a TV/laptop that phones join with a 4-letter code or QR. Started 2026-09-14 when Luqman asked for "another web party game" after scribble-relay.

Why this project exists

Luqman wanted a second party game. He picked Bluff Trivia over Imposter, Word Bomb and Forehead Guess, asked for both local and room play, aimed it at friends and family, and chose the retro TV game show look.

What counts as "done"

  1. A full game plays end to end in both modes.
  2. Room mode works on real phones over Supabase, including a phone reloading mid-game.
  3. Every built-in fact is true and sourced.
  4. Readable on a TV across the room and on a phone.

What is NOT in scope

  • Accounts, saved history, online leaderboards
  • AI-generated questions (no paid API key)
  • Audience voting / more than 10 players

How the game gets made

Pipeline

Bluff Show is a static web page with no build step. One rules file drives both ways to play, every built-in fact was researched with a source, and each change is proved by rules tests and by full games played in headless Chrome, which also take the screenshots on this page.

  1. Idea and scopingLuqman chose Bluff Trivia over Imposter, Word Bomb and Forehead Guess, with both ways to play, for friends and family, in a retro TV show look.01-idea.md · D-001
  2. Rules engineOne game state moves through write, pick, reveal and scores each round, then final. Scoring and the too-close-to-the-truth check live here, with no screen code.engine.js
  3. Sourced question bankSix research agents, one per category, checked every fact by web search and recorded a source URL; myths were dropped. 152 written, one duplicate removed.questions.js · D-004
  4. Screens and lookEvery screen for the three ways to use a device (pass-the-device, host, phone), styled as a 70s quiz show and sized up for TV screens.index.html · app.js
  5. Room modeThe host screen runs the rules and broadcasts a public view that hides the truth; phones send moves. Messages go over Supabase Realtime, or BroadcastChannel for tests.room.js · config.js · D-002, D-003
  6. Rules testsChecks the rules on their own: answer matching, custom questions, sitting out, scoring and awards.test/engine.test.js
  7. Browser tests and screenshotsPlays whole games through the real screens in headless Chrome at four sizes, then a room game with a TV tab and three phone tabs, saving screenshots on the way.test/run.sh · test/e2e.js · test/cdp.js
  8. Room mode live (next)Create the Supabase project in the dashboard, fill in config.js, publish on GitHub Pages and play a real game night on phones.03-milestones.md · M2, M3
  9. Project recordThis page, rebuilt from the notes, the screenshots and the git log whenever the game changes.tools/docs/build_docs.py

Screens

Screenshots from the game. Each carries the date it was taken: older ones show the game as it was then, and are kept as a record rather than replaced.

A pass-the-device game, on a laptop

One game in order, from setup to the podium, as the browser tests play it at 1440 x 900. The players are the test's Luqman, Aina, Hafiz and Siti, and the lies are the test's placeholder text, so they read like "Lie by Siti 1".

Room mode: the TV

The host screen at 1920 x 1080. It runs the rules and shows the game to the room; nobody types on it. The tests play this with one TV tab and three phone tabs talking over BroadcastChannel, because the Supabase project is not created yet.

Room mode: a player's phone

The same room game on Aina's phone. A phone only shows what the host sends it and sends back her moves, so it never knows the truth before the reveal.

The pass-the-device game again at iPhone size in portrait, where the game is most often played. Different questions from the laptop run, because each run draws its own.

A phone held sideways

Phone landscape, 844 x 390 points. The tests check nothing scrolls sideways; these show what fits on the first screen.

Tablet portrait, where the whole setup screen fits and the reveal has room to breathe.

01-idea.md · 4 sections

Idea

Problem

Luqman wanted another browser party game for friends and family, different in feel from scribble-relay (drawing telephone).

Proposed solution

Bluffing trivia. A strange-but-true question with a blank; each player writes a believable lie; all lies plus the truth are shown; players pick what they think is true. Points for finding the truth and for fooling people. Laughs come from the reveal: each lie that fooled someone is shown with who fell for it and who wrote it, then the truth with a one-line fact.

Extras chosen: "Need an idea?" gives a pre-written decoy lie; house decoys pad the board to 4 answers when there are few players; custom questions about people in the room, whose writer sits that round out; final round double; Master Liar and Truth Detective awards.

Target users

SegmentNeedWhy they'd pick us
Friends & family at homeA game for 3–10 people with no box and no appOpens in a browser; one phone is enough, or everyone's phone plus the TV

Alternatives considered (2026-09-14)

IdeaWhy not chosen
Imposter (secret word, one player doesn't know it)Was the recommendation; Luqman picked Bluff Trivia
Word Bomb (category + hidden timer, pass the phone)Not chosen
Forehead Guess (Heads Up with motion sensor)Phones only

06-decisions.md · 4 sections

Decisions

D-001 — Bluff Trivia, both modes, friends and family, retro TV show
  • Date: 2026-09-14
  • Status: active
  • Context: Luqman asked for another web party game and was asked what to build.
  • Decision: Bluff Trivia (not Imposter, which was recommended, nor Word Bomb or Forehead Guess). Both pass-one-device and join-a-room ("have both option"). Friends and family. Retro TV game show look.
  • Reversible? n/a — product direction
D-002 — Room mode over Supabase Realtime broadcast, not peer-to-peer
  • Date: 2026-09-14
  • Status: active
  • Options considered:
OptionProsCons
Supabase Realtime broadcastWorks on any network; no tables; static site stays staticNeeds a project and a key in config.js
PeerJS / WebRTCNo accountSome networks (school Wi-Fi, some carriers) block direct connections
  • Decision: Supabase, on a new project separate from Sky AI Brain so the memory database's key is never shipped in a public page. Luqman chose it.
  • Consequences: The publishable key sits in config.js in a public repo. That is what the key is for, and the project has no tables, so it can only relay messages. This is a deliberate exception to "no key values in code", recorded here.
D-003 — The host screen runs the rules; phones only send moves
  • Date: 2026-09-14
  • Status: active
  • Decision: One authoritative game state on the host. Phones send moves and render a public view the host broadcasts.
  • Reason: The same engine.js then drives both modes; there are no conflicting states between phones; nothing secret (truth, authors) is sent before the reveal.
  • Consequences: If the host tab closes, the game ends. The host keeps the screen awake with the Wake Lock API.
D-004 — Question bank written by six parallel research agents with sources
  • Date: 2026-09-14
  • Status: active
  • Decision: Six agents, one per category, each verifying every fact by web search and recording a source URL; myths and disputed facts were dropped (e.g. Frisbie Pie Company, Swiss 10pm toilet flushing, Lascaux dog). 152 written, one duplicate removed → 151.
  • Caveat: The Animals agent verified about 18 of its 26 from search result summaries rather than opening the page. Worth a spot-check before calling the bank final.

04-methods.md · 5 sections

Methods

Run and test
cd ~/Desktop/project/game/bluff-show
open index.html                         # pass-the-device mode works straight from the file
python3 -m http.server 8767             # then http://localhost:8767/?transport=local to try room mode in tabs
./test/run.sh                           # rules tests + full games in headless Chrome, screenshots in test/shots/
How the game is built (plain-language map)
  • engine.js is the rules and nothing else. One game state object moves through phases write → pick → reveal → scores per round, then final. Functions: submitLie, startPicking, submitPick, startReveal. Both modes call the same functions, so they cannot drift apart.
  • The host is the referee. In room mode the TV runs engine.js. Phones never hold the game; they send hello, lie, pick, idea and start messages and redraw from the state message the host sends back after every change, and every 3s.
  • publicView() is what goes over the air. While picking, it hides which answer is true and who wrote which lie.
  • A phone hides its own lie by comparing answer text with what it sent. After a reload it can't, so the host refuses the pick ("that's your own lie").
  • Moves are resent until confirmed, but only within the same round and phase. The host jumps to picking the moment the last lie arrives, so a pending move from a finished phase must be dropped (a bug caught by the tests on 2026-09-14).
  • A phone keeps its player ID in localStorage, so reloading and pressing Join again puts it back in the same seat.
  • "Too close to the truth" uses the question's answer plus alts, allowing 1–2 letter typos. Numbers must match exactly, so "81 years" is a valid lie when the truth is "116 years".
  • Room codes are 4 consonants, so a code can never spell a word.
Adding questions

Edit questions.js, one object per line: cat, q (with ____ once), a, alts, decoys (3 definitely-false), fact, source. cat must be one of CATS in app.js.

Testing pattern

test/cdp.js is the zero-dependency Chrome driver from scribble-relay (port 9342). Room mode is tested with ?transport=local, which swaps Supabase for the browser's BroadcastChannel so tabs talk to each other. Gotcha: test tabs share one localStorage, so they share bluff.pid; the reload test restores its own id first. Real phones don't have this problem.

The project record: docs/index.html (2026-09-15)

One HTML file holds the whole record of the game — overview, pipeline, captioned screenshots, idea, planning, milestones, decisions, methods, session logs, test files and git history — in the repo and on the documentation website. Luqman's standing rule: whenever the game changes, rebuild it and republish, the same as Referee For Fun.

python3 tools/docs/build_docs.py --publish

which rebuilds docs/index.html and then runs docs-site publish, putting it live at https://luqman-docs.netlify.app/bluff-show/ — the same link every time. These notes are read directly, so writing the knowledge base is most of updating the record. New screenshots need an entry in GALLERIES at the top of the script; a missing file shows as a labelled gap, not an error. Everything below the script's "engine" line is identical in all four game copies (auxetic-chess, bluff-show, kedai-runtuh, scribble-relay) — change it in all of them at once.

What proves it works, from each file's own header comment

Tests and tools

Tests

Run everything with ./test/run.sh: the rules tests first, then the browser games. Needs Node and Google Chrome.

FileWhat it does
test/run.shRules tests, then the whole game played in headless Chrome.
test/cdp.jsMinimal Chrome DevTools Protocol driver. No dependencies.
test/e2e.jsPlays Bluff Show through the real screens in headless Chrome: 1. a pass-the-device game at phone, tablet and desktop sizes 2. a room game: one host tab and three phone tabs, talking over BroadcastChannel (?transport=local) instead of Supabase
test/engine.test.jsChecks the rules on their own, without any screens. Run: node test/engine.test.js
The game's source files

The game itself, apart from index.html, which holds every screen and the whole look.

FileWhat it does
app.jsBluff Show — the screen flow. Three ways to use a device: mode 'local' — pass-one-device game. This device runs the rules. mode 'host' — the TV/laptop in room mode. This device runs the rules and sends everyone a view of the game after every change. mode 'phone' — a player's phone in room mode. It only shows what the host sent and sends back the player's moves.
config.jsRoom mode settings. Fill these in from the Supabase dashboard: Project Settings -> API Keys. The publishable key is designed to sit in web pages (it is not a secret), and this project has no tables, so the key can only relay game messages. Leave them empty and the game still works in pass-one-device mode.
engine.jsBluff Show — the rules of the game. No screen code lives here. The same rules run the pass-one-device mode and the room mode, where the host's screen runs them and phones only send moves. A game moves through phases: write -> every player secretly writes a fake answer pick -> everyone picks the answer they think is true reveal -> the lies that fooled someone are shown, then the truth scores -> the scoreboard; then the next round starts at "write" final -> after the last round
questions.jsBluff Show — the question bank. Each question is a strange-but-true fact with the answer blanked out as ____. cat the category shown on screen (must match a name in CATS in app.js) q the question, with ____ exactly once a the true answer, short alts other ways of writing the true answer, so nobody can enter it as a lie decoys three believable fake answers: "Need an idea?" hints, and fillers when there are too few lies on the board fact one sentence shown after the truth is revealed source where the fact was checked To add a question, copy a line, change it, and keep the comma at the end.
room.jsBluff Show — room mode messenger. Carries small messages between the host screen and the phones in a room. It knows nothing about the game rules: it only delivers messages. Normally messages travel through Supabase Realtime (a "broadcast" channel named after the room code). Add ?transport=local to the address to use the browser's own BroadcastChannel instead — tabs in one browser can then play a room with no internet, which is how the automated tests run room mode.
